results.controlIntent: Use [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] so as to: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Inform [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed changes to the system; and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed changes to the system that have not been approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Bar changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved changes to the system are completed.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from both CloudTrail and the model registry reveals multiple, serious violations of CM-3(1).r3:

**Violation 1 — CM-3(1)(d): Changes not barred until approval received.**
The `CreateEndpoint` event (evidence f7b3f679) fired at 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z. The only registry approval on record (evidence 19c78399) is timestamped 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z — two hours *before* the deployment. The CloudTrail note explicitly confirms the deployment preceded the approval gate. This means no automated mechanism barred the deployment until approval was in place; the approval and deployment ordering is inverted and the gate was ineffective.

**Violation 2 — CM-3(1)(e): Not all changes are documented.**
The `UpdateEndpoint` hotfix event (evidence 98e8dd22, 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z) has no corresponding model registry entry. This change was applied to the production endpoint without any registry-level documentation, directly violating the requirement to document *all* changes to the system.

**Violation 3 — CM-3(1)(a/b/c/f): No evidence of automated proposal, notification, or completion-notification mechanisms.**
Neither CloudTrail nor the registry shows any automated workflow for: (a) documenting proposed changes before execution, (b) notifying approval authorities of proposed changes, (c) highlighting changes pending approval beyond a defined time period, or (f) notifying personnel when approved changes are completed. The evidence shows ad-hoc, manual deployments by a single IAM user (data-scientist-jdoe) without a structured change-control pipeline.

In summary, the automated change-management control is not satisfied: the approval gate did not block deployment, a production change was entirely undocumented, and there is no evidence of the required automated notification and tracking mechanisms.
gaps: No evidence of an automated change-proposal workflow (e.g., ticketing system, SageMaker Pipeline approval step) that would satisfy CM-3(1)(a) and (b).
No evidence of an automated staleness/highlighting mechanism for unapproved changes beyond a defined time period (CM-3(1)(c)).
No evidence of automated completion-notification to designated personnel after approved changes are deployed (CM-3(1)(f)).
The hotfix UpdateEndpoint event has no registry entry — human attestation would be needed to determine whether any out-of-band approval process existed for this change.

It is unclear whether the 2-hour gap between approval (09:00) and deployment (11:00) reflects a broken gate or a misconfigured one — a review of the endpoint config and any CI/CD pipeline logs would clarify.
